strategies.name: support_to_resistance_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes, identify intraday support on the 5-minute chart using price action and moving averages such as the 13 EMA or, if that fails, the 200 EMA. Enter long when price comes down to that support area and bounces.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly into the next resistance or on the ensuing upward push; the speaker repeatedly frames the trade as getting in at support and selling at resistance without overstaying.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: use the 13 EMA as established support; enter when price taps/bounces from it
variants.target_note: exit on the quick upward move / at resistance
variants.transcript_quote: this 13 EMA operated as a initial support... the stock came down and it hit right there that's our entry for a scalp

variants.variant_label: 200 EMA deeper support bounce on 5-minute chart
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: after the 13 EMA loses support status, use the 200 EMA as deeper support and enter on the bounce
variants.target_note: ride it to resistance and exit
variants.transcript_quote: you get in here as support and you ride it to resistance and you exit okay another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA

result.enumeration_note: A short-after-support-break move is mentioned, but its exit is only gestured ('you want to exit right there') rather than taught as a repeatable rule, so it remains an unpromoted mention under Rule 1.
